 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. USC men's basketball was able to fend off a tough challenge from Wichita State late Sunday night in Nevada. Now the Trojans stay on the road and go up to the San Francisco Bay Area. The Men of Troy are in Berkeley to play former Pac-12 foe California in a crucial early-season game. USC has to be able to win a game like this to ensure it gets into the NCAA Tournament and boosts its chances of grabbing a relatively high seed.
 USC men's basketball is viewed by many analysts as a team capable of making the Sweet 16 this season. The Trojans should make the NCAA Tournament, but that isn't the goal this season. It is to win a couple of games and play on the second weekend of March Madness. USC has underachieved in the first two seasons of the Eric Musselman era. In order for the program to get back on schedule, merely reaching March Madness won't be nearly enough to satisfy fan expectations or, for that matter, the standards presented by those who follow and evaluate the program for a living. Musselman was an Elite Eight coach at Arkansas. Getting close to that standard is and should be the expectation for USC this season. If this really is a Sweet 16-caliber team, it should be able to handle its business against the Golden Bears.

 Cal 16, USC 14 - 10:35, 1st half
 11:25 PM ET, November 11 2026 
 USC players are simply rushing their shots and their offensive movements. Everyone needs to settle down. The defensive effort is decent but not exceptional. Cal has missed some open 3-pointers to keep the game close. When USC shares the ball, good things happen. The Trojans can't pound the dribble endlessly. Their offense has been stagnant at times.

 USC coughs up a bunch of turnovers and commits several silly fouls in the first four minutes. Very inattentive basketball from the Trojans. They need to lock in and focus on the little details.
 USC vs California injury updates
 09:50 PM ET, November 11 2026 
 Eric Reibe and Christian Collins, two players expected to be core rotational pieces for USC and Eric Musselman, have not played in either of the Trojans' first two games. They are expected to miss this game against Cal.
